\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.LearningTheory.FiniteFamily}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Labeled finite-family Fourier estimate]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p079-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b001
}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.ofCoefficients, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $m$ be a natural number, and for each $S\in\mathcal F$ provide
$m$ labeled samples consisting of a point of the Boolean cube and a sign. The resulting
sparse Fourier hypothesis has support $\mathcal F$ and assigns to each $S$ the empirical
Fourier coefficient computed from the samples for that $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite-family Fourier estimate from a target]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p079-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b001
}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube of dimension
$n$ to the signs, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and let $m$ be a natural number. Given $m$ cube inputs for each $S\in\mathcal F$, form
labeled samples by evaluating $f$ at those inputs, then use the labeled finite-family
Fourier estimator to produce the sparse Fourier hypothesis.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator hypothesis support]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_support}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and choose an input
in $\{-1,1\}^n$ for each member of $\mathcal{F}$ and each of $m$ sample indices. The
support of the resulting Fourier estimator hypothesis is exactly $\mathcal{F}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator output encoding and decoding]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_decode_encode}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_decode_encode}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.decode, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.decode_encode, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.encode, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and choose an input
in $\{-1,1\}^n$ for each member of $\mathcal{F}$ and each of $m$ sample indices.
Decoding the encoded Fourier estimator output formed from these inputs returns that same
output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator evaluation work]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_evaluationWork}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_evaluationWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.evaluationWork, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and choose an input
in $\{-1,1\}^n$ for each member of $\mathcal{F}$ and each of $m$ sample indices. For
every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the evaluation work of the resulting Fourier estimator
hypothesis at $x$ is $|\mathcal{F}|(n+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite-family estimator program with samples]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p079-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b001
}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $m$ be a natural number. The random-example learning program
draws $m$ independent uniform labeled examples for each member of $\mathcal F$, applies
the labeled finite-family Fourier estimator to the resulting matrix, and charges
$|\mathcal F|m(n+1)$ units of local work.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite-family Fourier estimator program]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p079-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b001
}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgramWithSamples, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon$ be a rational learning parameter with
$0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. The finite-family Fourier estimator program is the
random-example learning program that uses the sample count prescribed for $\mathcal F$
and $\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Law of the finite-family Fourier estimator]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixOutputLaw, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorLabeledOutput, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a target function, let $\mathcal
F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon$ be
a rational learning parameter with $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$. The estimator program's
outcome law is the law obtained by drawing an independent uniform batch of the
prescribed sample size for each $S\in\mathcal F$ and returning the hypothesis whose
coefficient at $S$ is the empirical Fourier coefficient from that batch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator program exact cost]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixOutputLaw, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.runWithCost_finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$ be rational. Every outcome in the support of the estimator
program's output-and-cost distribution has cost
$(|\mathcal{F}|M,0,|\mathcal{F}|M+|\mathcal{F}|M(n+1))$, where the three entries count
random examples, queries, and work, respectively, and $M$ is the prescribed number of
samples per coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator program cost components]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_components}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_components}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_eq, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$ be rational. For every outcome in the support of the estimator
program's output-and-cost distribution, the number of random examples is
$|\mathcal{F}|M$, the number of queries is zero, and the work is
$|\mathcal{F}|M+|\mathcal{F}|M(n+1)$, where $M$ is the program's prescribed number of
samples per coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure bits for a finite family]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientFailureBits_eq}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientFailureBits_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidence, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. If the confidence parameter is $1/(10|\mathcal{F}|)$,
then the number of failure bits is $\lceil\log_2(20|\mathcal{F}|)\rceil$, where this
expression is interpreted as the least integer $k$ with $2^k\ge 20|\mathcal{F}|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Samples per coefficient bound]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientAccuracy, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidence, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_cast_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. Put $\delta=1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, $\eta=\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal
F|)$, and let $L$ be the least integer $k$ such that $2^k\geq\lceil 2/\delta\rceil$. If
$N=\lceil 2L/\eta^2\rceil$ is the sample count per coefficient, then $N\leq 16|\mathcal
F|^2L/\varepsilon^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total random examples bound]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyTotalRandomExamples_cast_le}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyTotalRandomExamples_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidence, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient_cast_le, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. Put $\delta=1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, $\eta=\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal
F|)$, and let $L$ be the least integer $k$ such that $2^k\geq\lceil 2/\delta\rceil$. If
$N=\lceil 2L/\eta^2\rceil$ is the sample count per coefficient, then the total number
$|\mathcal F|N$ of random examples satisfies $|\mathcal F|N\leq 16|\mathcal
F|^3L/\varepsilon^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total work bound]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyTotalWork_cast_le}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyTotalWork_cast_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidence, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.finiteFamilyTotalRandomExamples_cast_le, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. Put $\delta=1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, $\eta=\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal
F|)$, and let $L$ be the least integer $k$ such that $2^k\geq\lceil 2/\delta\rceil$. If
$N=\lceil 2L/\eta^2\rceil$ is the sample count per coefficient, then $|\mathcal
F|N+|\mathcal F|N(n+1)\leq 16|\mathcal F|^3(n+2)L/\varepsilon^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator program polynomial cost bound]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_polyBound}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b001}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_polyBound}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientFailureBits_eq, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorProgram_cost_components, FABL.finiteFamilyTotalRandomExamples_cast_le, FABL.finiteFamilyTotalWork_cast_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$ be rational. For every outcome in the support of the estimator
program's output-and-cost distribution, its number of random examples, viewed as a
rational number, is at most
$16|\mathcal{F}|^3\lceil\log_2(20|\mathcal{F}|)\rceil/\varepsilon^2$; its number of
queries is zero; and its work, viewed as a rational number, is at most
$16|\mathcal{F}|^3(n+2)\lceil\log_2(20|\mathcal{F}|)\rceil/\varepsilon^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product measure for a uniform sample matrix]
\lean{FABL.uniformSampleMatrix_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\label{FABL.uniformSampleMatrix_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixInputLaw, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of the
$n$ coordinate indices. The measure associated with a uniform random matrix indexed by
$\mathcal F$, with each row consisting of $m$ inputs from $\{−1,1\}^n$, is the product
over $S\in\mathcal F$ of the measures associated with uniform random $m$-tuples of such
inputs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parameterized coefficient bad set]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSetWithParameters}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSetWithParameters}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite
family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $a,c$ be rational parameters with
$0<a,c\le 1/2$. For $S\in\mathcal F$, the bad set consists of sample arrays assigning to
every member of $\mathcal F$ a batch of $m$ cube inputs, where $m$ is the estimator
sample count for $(a,c)$, such that the absolute difference between the empirical
Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$ from its assigned batch and the true Fourier
coefficient of $f$ on $S$ is at least $a$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, and
let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$. Let the accuracy and
confidence parameters each be rational numbers in $(0,1/2]$, and choose any
$S\in\mathcal F$. Draw uniformly an array of independent Boolean-cube inputs indexed
by $\mathcal F$ and by the estimator's sample indices, whose sample count is determined
by those accuracy and confidence parameters. The probability that the empirical Fourier
coefficient at $S$ differs from the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ by at least the
accuracy parameter is at most the confidence parameter.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Any coefficient failure bound]
\lean{FABL.measure_finiteFamily_someCoefficientBadSetWithParameters_le}
\label{FABL.measure_finiteFamily_someCoefficientBadSetWithParameters_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.randomExampleMatrixInputLaw, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSetWithParameters, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.measure_finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSetWithParameters_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, let
$\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$, and let the accuracy and
confidence parameters be rational numbers in $(0,1/2]$. Draw uniformly an array of
Boolean-cube samples indexed by $\mathcal F$, with sample count determined by those
parameters. The probability that at least one empirical Fourier coefficient indexed by
$S\in\mathcal F$ differs from its true coefficient by at least the accuracy parameter
is at most $|\mathcal F|$ times the confidence parameter.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite-family coefficient bad set]
\lean{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSet}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002}
\label{FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientAccuracy, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSetWithParameters, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientConfidence, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a
nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb
Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. For $S\in\mathcal F$, the bad set consists of arrays
assigning to each member of $\mathcal F$ a batch of $m$ cube inputs, where $m$ is the
sample count obtained using accuracy $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$ and confidence
$1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, for which the empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ differs from
its true coefficient by at least $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$.
\end{definition}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b006}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, and
let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $[n]$. Let $\varepsilon$ be
a rational accuracy parameter in $(0,1/2]$, and choose any $S\in\mathcal F$. Draw
uniformly an array of Boolean-cube samples indexed by $\mathcal F$, with the sample
count specified by $\mathcal F$ and $\varepsilon$. The probability that the empirical
Fourier coefficient at $S$ differs from its true Fourier coefficient by at least the
accuracy assigned to $\mathcal F$ and $\varepsilon$ is at most the confidence assigned
to $\mathcal F$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of the $n$ coordinates,
and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq\frac12$. Suppose the sum
of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ outside $\mathcal{F}$ is at most
$\varepsilon/2$. Suppose also that each rational coefficient assigned to a set in
$\mathcal{F}$ differs from the corresponding Fourier coefficient of $f$ by at most
$\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal{F}|)$. The Boolean function obtained by taking the sign of the
resulting sparse Fourier sum, with nonnegative values assigned sign $+1$, has relative
Hamming distance at most $\varepsilon$ from $f$.
\end{theorem}

}
\label{FABL.relativeHammingDist_finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput_le_of_no_bad}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.evaluate, FABL.SparseFourierHypothesis.ofCoefficients, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff_cast, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientAccuracy, FABL.finiteFamilyCoefficientBadSet, FABL.finiteFamilyFourierEstimatorOutput, FABL.finiteFamilySamplesPerCoefficient, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.relativeHammingDist_sparseFourierHypothesis_of_coefficients_le}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube $\{−1,1\}^n$, let $\mathcal H$ be a
nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $0<\varepsilon\le
1/2$. For each $S\in\mathcal H$, take the prescribed number of sample inputs, and form
the Fourier estimator whose coefficient at $S$ is the empirical average of
$f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$. If the Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\mathcal H$ is at most
$\varepsilon/2$, and every estimated coefficient differs from its true Fourier
coefficient by strictly less than $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal H|)$, then the Boolean
function obtained by taking the sign of the estimated Fourier sum has relative Hamming
distance at most $\varepsilon$ from $f$.
\end{theorem}
